name: King Saul
charge: Offering the burnt offering himself at Gilgal; sparing Agag and the best of the spoil; and stubbornness, which is as iniquity and idolatry
summary: The first king of Israel began to show his simplicity at Gilgal: told to wait seven days until Samuel came, he panicked when the people scattered, offered the burnt offering that was not his office to offer, and answered the prophet with excuses. Sent to wipe out Amalek, he spared Agag and the best of the flocks, greeted Samuel claiming he had carried out the Lord’s command while the sheep were bleating in the prophet’s ears, and laid it on the people. Obeying counts for more than sacrifice, and rebellion ranks with witchcraft. The kingdom was torn from him that day, and it ended on mount Gilboa.
offenseFull: Chapter thirteen is the beginning of Saul showing his simplicity, the proof he was not fit to be king. Samuel had told him to wait seven days at Gilgal (1 Samuel 10:8). When the Philistines massed, the chosen nation hid in caves and pits, though the Lord had just defeated the Philistines for them; the spirit God gives is not fear but power, love and self-control (2 Timothy 1:7). With Samuel not yet come and the people scattering, Saul offered the burnt offering himself, Samuel’s office, not his, and Samuel arrived as he finished (1 Samuel 13:8-14). Brothers do the same today: leadership said ten o’clock, it is five past, so we go home. Wait as you were instructed; the Lord may be testing your patience, and a man is not to rush in time of trouble (Ecclesiasticus 2:2).

Then came the excuses: the people scattering, Samuel late, the Philistines gathering. That is the pattern of the man; he never holds himself accountable, he always deflects, going out to meet the man before he gets to where he messed up. Samuel told him he had acted foolishly and his kingdom would not last, for the Lord had sought a man after His own heart (Acts 13:22). Disobeying the prophet’s instruction was disobeying the commandment of the Lord.

Then Saul was sent to destroy Amalek completely for what it did to Israel on the way out of Egypt (1 Samuel 15:3), the war sworn from generation to generation (Exodus 17:16; Deuteronomy 25:17-19). Christianity says forgive and forget; the Most High said remember. But Saul spared Agag and the best of the flocks, destroying only what was worthless (1 Samuel 15:9), killing what looked like it deserved killing so he could say he did some killing. Saul did most of it, and the Lord counted that as not carrying out His commands at all (1 Samuel 15:10-11). Whenever there is a but in your obedience, you did not perform the orders given to you. At Carmel he raised a monument to himself, then claimed he had obeyed while sheep bleated nearby, and blamed the people, as at Gilgal. The Lord’s commands are kept with nothing added or taken away (Deuteronomy 12:32). Still insisting he had obeyed, he boasted of bringing back Agag; a man who justifies himself is condemned by his own mouth (Job 9:20).
judgmentFull: Samuel made it plain: the Lord delights in obedience more than in burnt offerings (1 Samuel 15:22). Spoil taken against His will made the offering ridiculous; the sacrifice of the wicked is detestable, worse when brought with evil intent (Proverbs 21:27). Rebellion ranks with witchcraft and stubbornness with idolatry, and because Saul rejected the Lord’s word, the Lord rejected him as king (1 Samuel 15:23). A brother who would never touch voodoo will sit through a whole counsel of do not do this and call two weeks later saying he did it anyway, and according to this verse that rebellion is witchcraft. Stubbornness is idolatry because the instruction is the Lord’s commandment carried by leadership, and stubbornness against it puts what I want before what God wants.

The confession finally came and was still not sincere: he feared the people and did what they said (1 Samuel 15:24). Fear of man is a trap, but whoever trusts the Lord is safe (Proverbs 29:25); a leader in fear of his people is being led by them. Saul tore Samuel’s robe, and Samuel told him the Lord had torn the kingdom from him that day for a better man; God does not lie or change His mind (Numbers 23:19). Then he asked to be honoured before the elders anyway, hiding the demotion: the spirit of vanity, caught up in a title and forgetting it came for pleasing the Lord.

Samuel mourned for him, for he had seen his potential. The Spirit of the Lord left Saul and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him (1 Samuel 16:14), and instead of repenting he went down into envy of David. It all traces back to bashfulness: he looked in the mirror and saw a kitty cat where God had said there was a lion, self-willed because he was afraid, and would not ask, wait or take counsel with the prophet at his side. A man can ruin his own soul through bashfulness and bring himself down by respecting persons (Ecclesiasticus 20:22). At the end, with the Lord silent, he consulted a medium, the very thing he had driven out of the land, and heard that he and his sons would die the next day (1 Samuel 28:19). They fell on mount Gilboa, Saul on his own sword (1 Samuel 31:4-6), dying for his unfaithfulness and for seeking a medium, and the kingdom went to David (1 Chronicles 10:13).

text.text: And thou shalt go down before me to Gilgal; and, behold, I will come down unto thee, to offer burnt offerings, and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings: seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee, and shew thee what thou shalt do.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
And he tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him.
And Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering.
And it came to pass, that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him, that he might salute him.

And Samuel said, What hast thou done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that thou camest not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash;
Therefore said I, The Philistines will come down now upon me to Gilgal, and I have not made supplication unto the Lord: I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering.

And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God, which he commanded thee: for now would the Lord have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.

But now thy kingdom shall not continue: the Lord hath sought him a man after his own heart, and the Lord hath commanded him to be captain over his people, because thou hast not kept that which the Lord commanded thee.
Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.

And when he had removed him, he raised up unto them David to be their king; to whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will.
Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.
For he said, Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt;
How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.

Therefore it shall be, when the Lord thy God hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it, that thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it.

But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, and of the oxen, and of the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not utterly destroy them: but every thing that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly.
Then came the word of the Lord unto Samuel, saying,
It repenteth me that I have set up Saul to be king: for he is turned back from following me, and hath not performed my commandments. And it grieved Samuel; and he cried unto the Lord all night.
What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.
If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.
And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?
For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.
And Saul said unto Samuel, I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.
The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe.
God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?
But the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him.
There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.

Moreover the Lord will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me: the Lord also shall deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.

Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.
And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him.
So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together.

So Saul died for his transgression which he committed against the Lord, even against the word of the Lord, which he kept not, and also for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it;
